item.title: Wiley Convicted In Netherlands Over Antisemitic Posts, Campaign Group Says
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiley's Dutch case ends in convictions without punishment, the group behind the complaint says, six years after his posts.
item.content:encoded:
Wiley has been convicted in the Netherlands over his antisemitic social media posts, but the court imposed no punishment because of the time that had passed, according to the organization that pursued the case.

Campaign Against Antisemitism announced the outcome on November 17, identifying the offenses as group defamation and incitement to violence under Dutch law.

The charity said Dutch prosecutors received its lawyers’ complaint after British police established that Wiley had been outside the U.K. when he posted the messages in July 2020.

The group said the messages attacked Jewish people collectively and called for violence. It credited Dutch lawyer Ronnie Eisenmann with pursuing the complaint and the Community Security Trust with helping establish Wiley’s location.

“He has now been convicted of group defamation and incitement to violence in The Netherlands,” said Stephen Silverman, the charity’s director of investigations and enforcement.

Wiley’s posts had already cost him professional relationships and access to major social platforms.

His longtime manager, John Woolf, ended their working relationship, and Facebook, Instagram and Twitter removed his accounts during the original controversy. Twitter also apologized for the time it took to respond before permanently suspending his account.

As AllHipHop reported at the time, Wiley later offered an apology while insisting the dispute should have stayed between him and his manager.

“My comments should not have been directed to all Jews or Jewish people,” Wiley said in an interview with Sky News.

“I’m not racist, you know. I’m a businessman,” he said.

The interview also included his offer to give up his MBE, an honor he had received for services to music in 2018, as calls grew for it to be withdrawn. “Take it back,” he said.

The East London MC helped build grime through Roll Deep, the crew that also included Dizzee Rascal before the two artists fell out.

Their relationship eventually improved enough for an onstage reunion at a Dubai concert in 2023.

“Antisemites do not stop at national borders and neither will we in pursuing them,” Silverman said when CAA announced its Dutch complaint in 2020.

Wiley later lost his MBE in February 2024, with the Cabinet Office citing bringing the honors system into disrepute.

item.title: Erica Campbell Hires Security After Unwanted Visits & Slashed Tires
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Erica Campbell says repeated visits to her home have prompted police calls and private security as she shares doorbell video.
item.content:encoded:
Erica Campbell says private security is part of her family’s response to repeated unwanted visits at their home, where she has shared footage of a woman at the door.

The Mary Mary singer has contacted the LAPD several times, according to TMZ, which reported on the videos and her account of the situation.

“I’m covered and protected, but I ain’t got no reason to lie to nobody for nothing,” Campbell wrote in her Instagram caption.

Her account includes a call from her daughter, who told her through FaceTime that a woman was in the backyard. Campbell said the visitor had appeared at the house before.

The videos described in the report show encounters at the entrance, including a woman attempting to communicate through a window. Campbell had previously told her church congregation that someone allegedly slashed the family’s tires.

She has described the situation as “not a joke” and “not a game,” while saying she has also sought help through mental health channels.

Campbell has spent much of her career bringing gospel into spaces shared with rap and R&B. Her recent work includes Skilla Baby’s “Strength in Numbers”, a song addressing poverty and violence on his album The Price of Fame.

That project arrived in August with other guests including Nas, Chris Brown and Bryson Tiller. Skilla has spoken about using the album to work through his own struggles after surviving a shooting.

David Banner also named Campbell among the collaborators on The God Box 2, alongside vocalists Anthony Hamilton, Raheem DeVaughn and Eric Bellinger. Those appearances extend a catalog that already reaches beyond her recordings with Mary Mary.

She and her sister Tina broke through with Thankful in 2000. Campbell later established a solo career with Help, which debuted atop the Top Gospel Albums chart and reached No. 6 on the Billboard 200.

Her first solo single, “A Little More Jesus,” earned a Grammy nomination before that album arrived.

The song also earned writing nominations for Tina and Warryn, keeping the family’s creative partnership intact even as Campbell stepped out with her own solo material.

Campbell and her husband, producer Warryn Campbell, married in 2001.

item.title: Wyclef Jean & Lauryn Hill Bring Clipse To Brooklyn For ‘The Score’ Anniversary
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Wyclef Jean and Lauryn Hill book Brooklyn with Clipse, family ties and a ticket donation attached to The Score's anniversary.
item.content:encoded:
Wyclef Jean and Lauryn Hill are bringing “The Score” back to Brooklyn, with Clipse opening their December 17 anniversary concert at Barclays Center.

For Hill, the location connects the Fugees’ music to family history and a departed friend. She explained that connection in a statement announcing the show.

Hill said: “Brooklyn is woven into our story. It’s where my mother was born, where Wyclef first landed after leaving Haiti, and where our brother John Forté, RIP, called home. There’s something about Brooklyn that has always resonated with us: its spirit, its people, its music, and its ability to uniquely reflect culture while moving the world. The love has always been mutual, and we’ve never forgotten that. Brooklyn in the ’90s was something else! We’re beyond excited to celebrate this anniversary in Brooklyn.”

The one-night event celebrates 30 years of the Fugees’ second album. Pusha T and Malice will perform as Clipse, with additional guests still to be announced.

“Thirty years on, The Score still sounds past, present and future,” Wyclef said. “We made a vow to ourselves as teenagers that music is only the byproduct of the movement. We said we would be the voice of the voiceless. Young or old, we will forever cross generations. That’s what a classic does. It doesn’t age, it just keeps finding new ears. Our job is to make sure the world keeps hearing it, and that the next generation gets to discover it for the first time.”

The Brooklyn booking follows the pair’s announced Miami Art Week appearance, extending a run built around the album. Their anniversary performances have already included Lisbon and Paris.

Released in 1996, “The Score” brought “Ready or Not,” “Fu-Gee-La” and “Killing Me Softly” to a worldwide audience. The Fugees won two Grammys the following year, including Best Rap Album. The album also reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

Organizers say tickets go on sale November 19 at 10 A.M. Eastern through Ticketmaster. The December 17 performance is scheduled for 8 P.M., with Jay Upscale and Global Citizen partnering on the event.

One dollar from each ticket will go to the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund.

item.title: Camp Flog Gnaw Gets Praise & Plenty Criticism
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Camp Flog Gnaw’s value gets questioned after alleged repetitive performances, merchandise overload and Tyler's large security.
item.content:encoded:
I promise. This is the top level of what a source conveyed. My editor’s said, “No” to revealing everything seen and said.

Tyler, The Creator might want to check the Camp Flog Gnaw suggestion box. A source close by said the carnival may want to get some new rides.

The festival returned to Dodger Stadium on November 14 and 15, but an attendee who spoke with AllHipHop says Saturday left them questioning whether the experience still justified the expense.

READ ALSO: Tyler, The Creator’s Sold-Out Camp Flog Gnaw Streams Live…

“It was pretty much just a money grab,” the source said. They were a VIP too.

Whew.

Don Toliver’s performance was among their biggest grievances. The source said one song came around five times, as in he performed the same song consecutively. Admittedly, others that reviewed the show did not have that experience. Same festival, very different ride home. It also may be an age thing. I dunno.

There were bright spots. Leon Thomas and JID were praised and apparently got all the audience engagement too. Glad to hear they had the chutzpah to serve all in attendance.

Then came the complaints about the grounds. If you were not buying a lot, you may not have been interested, because the merchandise presence was heavy, They could not locate the journalist interview area at all.

“And if it was if it existed, I don’t know where the hell it was,” the source said.

The credentials may have changed, or something or maybe they deliberately excluded journalists. We do not know since we were not there.

Tyler is a star. This is the part I am not so sure about. Tyler was not so close to fans and those that adore him. He was not so readily available and surrounded by a lot of security.

READ ALSO: Freddie Gibbs And Alchemist Have Another Helping Of Alfredo On The Way…

“I mean I guess it means he’s a human being,” they said.

Let’s get to the ticket prices. The official website lists starting prices of $415 for general admission, $725 for VIP and $1,750 for Super VIP. Lawdie. I’d definitely be sitting outside of the venue and try to hear some stray sounds.

Has Camp Flog Gnaw become so polished as a shopping destination that some fans are missing the gathering they originally loved? That’s what I am gathering and I can relate. We were front line on stuff like The Roots Picnic and AfroPunk. Not a shred of hate, but they are very different now than when they started.

Hip-Hop fans will buy the shirt. A journalist or an industry person may not. That may be the big difference here.

item.title: Wale Plans Thanksgiving Food Drive For Gifted Week Finale
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wale puts a holiday food drive on Gifted Week's final-day schedule as his DMV community program returns for its third year.
item.content:encoded:
Wale is putting a Thanksgiving food drive on the closing-day schedule for Gifted Week, with a three-hour event planned for families in the Washington area.

The holiday drive is scheduled for November 20 from 10 A.M. to 1 P.M., according to WKYS. It falls on the final day of the rapper’s third annual community program, which he organizes with his management company, EQT.

The station lists Friday’s theme as “Service Is a Gift.” A sneaker and jersey design workshop follows that evening, running from 5 P.M. to 7 P.M.

This year’s four-day program carries an “Ambition” theme, marking 15 years since Wale released the album. Its schedule brings together educational activities, sports programming and opportunities for young creatives from Washington, Maryland and Virginia.

WKYS directs people interested in attending to Wale’s Instagram account, @wale, for registration information and further announcements. Some activities require registration, while the opening reception was listed as invitation-only.

The food drive adds a holiday-service component to a week that also includes a career panel featuring Black sports professionals.

That November 19 event pairs the Washington Nationals with Diverse Representation at the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library.

Attendees will have a chance to hear how executives, agents and other industry figures built careers away from the playing field. A networking reception is also planned as part of the program.

The November 18 workshop at Howard University centers on a film panel with six executives from music and sports, giving participants another setting to discuss their creative ideas.

Wale has used earlier editions to connect his music audience with local youth activities. In 2024, Gifted Week included a Nike sneaker design workshop, a Commanders football clinic, poetry and a discussion about music and sports.

That edition coincided with his Every Blue Moon Tour’s homecoming stop at MGM National Harbor. It followed his 2023 Kennedy Center concert celebrating the 10th anniversary of The Gifted, when Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser designated November 10 as Wale Day.

The current schedule also includes a sports media and culture film workshop from 6:30 P.M. to 8 P.M. on November 18.

item.title: Rod Wave’s Lawyers Challenge Indictment Ahead Of Atlanta Concerts
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Rod Wave's defense answers the indictment with a court challenge while pointing to his album success and Atlanta concerts.
item.content:encoded:
Rod Wave‘s lawyers are pushing back against his Georgia indictment as the rapper prepares for two Atlanta concerts, arguing the case has not interrupted his career.

In a statement to TMZ, attorneys Marissa Goldberg, Drew Findling and Zack Findling disputed the charges and pointed to his work since the underlying arrest. They cited a No. 1 album debut and a national tour they described as sold out.

“We look forward to vigorously challenging this baseless indictment and the clear violations of Mr. Green’s rights in court,” the attorneys said. They maintained that the charges remained no more valid than before.

The defense described the indictment as a formal charging document arising from the same incident, rather than a new encounter with police. Their response followed news of the indictment on drug possession, firearm and reckless-driving charges.

State Farm Arena lists Rod Wave’s Don’t Look Down Tour for November 18 and 19, with Fridayy as the special guest. The lawyers specifically highlighted those Atlanta dates in their statement, calling both performances sold out.

The traffic-stop case began November 7, 2025, when an Atlanta officer accused Rod Wave of driving through a stop sign on Defoor Avenue NW. The officer estimated his speed at 45 mph in a 30 mph zone.

An arrest warrant previously reported by Atlanta News First said the officer followed him to a QuikTrip parking lot on Howell Mill Road. The officer then arrested him for reckless driving and reported finding a handgun during a pat-down. The warrant said he had delayed activating his lights and siren because he suspected the vehicle’s driver might try to flee.

The warrant also recorded a different account from passenger Jamond Byner, who told police the pair left a recording studio and disputed the reckless driving charge. Police arrested Byner during the same encounter.

Rod Wave was released the next day on an $8,000 bond. His lawyers had challenged the arrest before the indictment, accusing police of targeting the rapper.

A separate case concerns an April 2025 incident at his Milton home; his attorneys have maintained he was a burglary victim.

The Atlanta concerts are scheduled to begin at 8 P.M.

item.title: Jay-Z’s Firm Leads $28 Million Hone Health Investment As Clinic Expands
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jay-Z's MarcyPen leads Hone Health's $28 million equity raise as the clinic expands, following Roc Nation-backed Duetti's deal.
item.content:encoded:
Jay-Z‘s MarcyPen Capital Partners is leading a $28 million investment in Hone Health as the online clinic expands beyond its roots in men’s hormone care.

The equity raise extends Hone’s Series A. It sits alongside $200 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund, bringing the new financing to $228 million, Dealroom reported.

General Catalyst’s money covers sales and marketing costs and gets repaid from revenue generated by new customers. The $28 million equity investment is the portion led by MarcyPen.

Other backers include Gwyneth Paltrow’s Kinship Ventures, Pentland Ventures, Hanwha, Gannet Capital and Humbition. Kelly Rowland and the Jonas Brothers are among the individual investors.

“Saad and the team at Hone are proven business builders dedicated to making it easier for people to live better, healthier lives,” Jay Brown said.

Hone launched in 2020 with hormone care and has expanded into preventive services for men and women. The company says it has treated about 200,000 patients and surpassed $100 million in recurring revenue last year.

Its earlier $33 million Series A announcement outlined that expansion through telemedicine, laboratory testing and personalized treatment plans. Hone also acquired ivee, bringing clinicians into patients’ homes rather than limiting appointments to a screen.

At that stage, Hone reported 300,000 people tested and 55,000 treated. Its approach combined prescriptions with guidance on diet, exercise, sleep and stress.

“The next decade will completely rewrite how we live our life from our 30s well into our 100s,” CEO Saad Alam said in that announcement.

The healthcare investment follows Duetti’s $665 million financing announcement. Roc Nation is an existing investor in the music-rights company, which buys and manages independent catalogs.

Duetti’s release identifies a $450 million asset-backed securitization anchored by Carlyle, $165 million in Viola Credit capacity and a $50 million facility from Flexpoint Ford and Truist Bank.

Carlyle’s Akhil Bansal said “independent music royalties can generate the kind of recurring, diversified cash flows that asset-backed finance is built around.”

Duetti says it has completed more than 1,600 catalog investments and holds over 50,000 masters and compositions, representing more than 3,000 recording artists.

Duetti plans to use that capital to expand its catalog investments across more genres and countries.

item.title: Vinny Cha$e Dies As Kid Art Mourns Harlem Rapper
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Vinny Cha$e's creative partner remembers the Cheers Club artist's influence on music and style after announcing his death.
item.content:encoded:
Vinny Cha$e has died, according to his longtime collaborator Kid Art, who announced the Harlem rapper’s death in an emotional Instagram tribute. Kid Art said a car accident claimed his friend’s life.

The statement came from a partner who helped build Cheers Club alongside him through years of recording and other creative work. Kid Art remembered the partnership as a friendship that reached well beyond recording songs.

“One of the most special souls we’ve ever known, he gave so much to us and to the game,” Kid Art wrote.

He credited Vinny’s personality and approach to fashion with influencing other careers. He also expressed gratitude that listeners had recently heard new music from the rapper before his death.

Their creative relationship stretched back to Vinny’s earliest steps behind a microphone. In an interview, Vinny recalled spending roughly six months practicing privately before letting people hear what he could do.

Kid Art and Cartier encouraged him to move forward. Vinny had already been interested in clothing and design, and rapping became another outlet rather than a replacement for those pursuits.

He described Cheers Club as a business that could accommodate records, production, films and clothing. The group’s members handled those projects themselves, keeping the different parts of their business together.

Vinny’s introduction to the industry came through video work around Juelz Santana and Dipset. He later signed with Epic through Cheers Club, bringing his collective into the label deal.

He also recorded a mixtape with Soulja Boy, explaining that the collaboration introduced his work to a different audience. Among his own projects, he singled out Survival of the Swag for the way it came together within his team.

Harlem remained central to how he explained himself.

AllHipHop previously covered his neighborhood tour for Life+Times, where he discussed new housing, chain stores and the pressure on local businesses.

He acknowledged that redevelopment could displace some shops while arguing that others had relationships strong enough to endure. The tour also gave him space to explain Cheers Club beyond the songs.

Vinny traced his interest in fashion to his grandfather, who worked as a tailor in Trinidad.

item.title: Alicia Keys Reportedly In Talks To Join Jay-Z’s Super Bowl Show
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Alicia Keys enters the guest conversation for Jay-Z's halftime show as a report describes talks and floats John Legend's name.
item.content:encoded:
Alicia Keys could reunite with Jay-Z on the Super Bowl stage, with a new report placing her in talks about a guest appearance. Their “Empire State of Mind” partnership now has a possible halftime sequel.

Sources told Page Six that Keys has discussed joining the rapper for his February 14, 2027, performance at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The outlet also mentioned John Legend, though his involvement was described only as “being whispered about.”

Representatives for all three artists did not comment to Page Six. The report leaves Keys’ appearance at the discussion stage, with no confirmed guest booking announced.

Both singers work with Roc Nation, the company behind the halftime production. Keys and Jay-Z already share a signature New York anthem, while Legend performed “God Did” with him at SoFi during October’s anniversary concerts.

Legend had previously said he had not received a halftime invitation. In an interview with Fadam Got Da Juice, he backed Jay-Z’s ability to perform without guests and praised the depth of his catalog.

Those comments preceded the new report. Legend’s connection to Roc Nation also extends beyond a concert appearance: he moved his music management to the company earlier this year, with Jay Brown taking over after his departure from Friends at Work. His former manager, Ty Stiklorius, said she would continue working with him on business ventures they had built together during their long partnership.

Keys has already shared a Super Bowl halftime stage with another longtime collaborator. She joined Usher at the February 11, 2024, game in Las Vegas, opening her appearance at the piano with “If I Ain’t Got You.”

The pair then sang “My Boo,” their duet from 2004. That show also brought out Ludacris, Lil Jon and H.E.R., with Keys among the guests woven into Usher’s career-spanning performance at Allegiant Stadium.

Jay-Z’s own announcement followed a stadium run celebrating his debut album’s 30th anniversary. “From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” he said.

“My Boo” earned Keys and Usher a Grammy for best R&B performance by a duo or group with vocals.

item.title: Jamaica Ja’Toi Dies As “Baby Boy” Viewers Remember His $40 Scene
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jamaica Ja'Toi is remembered by TS Madison as his work with John Singleton reaches far beyond the familiar salon scene.
item.content:encoded:
Jamaica Ja’Toi has died, with TS Madison paying tribute to the screen actor whose brief encounter with Tyrese in “Baby Boy” became a familiar part of the film’s afterlife.

Madison posted a memorial on her official YouTube channel on November 16, honoring a friend she had also interviewed about his career. She credited him with connecting her with Mo’Nique and Sidney, remembering the relationships he built outside his screen work.

“You were a light in this Dark world,” Madison wrote in the tribute. “I’ll never forget you,” she added.

Ja’Toi, also known as Jamaica Carter, worked as John Singleton’s executive assistant before the director put him in front of the camera. In an interview with Madison for FOX SOUL, he explained that Singleton already knew his sense of humor from their everyday exchanges.

The invitation to join “Baby Boy” came the day before filming, he recalled. Singleton asked him to arrive dressed like someone who worked in a hair salon, turning their working relationship into an unexpected acting opportunity.

Ja’Toi remembered being nervous and repeating the scene for the camera. The resulting exchange put him opposite Tyrese’s character Jody, negotiating over an outfit and delivering the incredulous “$40” reaction associated with his role.

His account of Singleton focused just as much on what happened away from the set. Ja’Toi said the filmmaker taught him about advertising costs, music licensing, editing and working with lawyers, exposing him to the decisions behind a movie’s release.

“I miss him. I think about him all the time,” Ja’Toi told Madison.

“Baby Boy” followed Jody, an unemployed young father still living with his mother in South Central Los Angeles.

The story follows the pressures of parenthood, his relationship with Yvette and the arrival of his mother’s boyfriend Melvin. Tyrese shared the cast with Taraji P. Henson, Ving Rhames, A.J. Johnson and Snoop Dogg, who played Rodney.

The film also remained a reference point for its lead actors. Henson later discussed how her career and Tyrese’s diverged after their work with Singleton, as he moved into major movie franchises.

Sony Pictures released “Baby Boy” in 2001.
